tonight.headline: Golden and Love still limited; Jacobs practised and is off the report
body: Bad news first: Rashee Rice did not practise Wednesday (hamstring/knee, Chiefs.com 21 Oct) and stays priced at 0.0. Matthew Golden (shoulder) and his quarterback Jordan Love (back) were both limited; Love says it is 'a sore back from the game' and he is not worried about missing Detroit (Packers Wire 22 Oct).

Better: Josh Jacobs practised and is not on Green Bay's injury report; Ian Rapoport expects him to play (Packernet 22 Oct), though LaFleur has said his carries may be managed. ESPN has you 55%, 122.7 to Furia Regia's 113.0. The projection lineup is 0.9 higher with Jacobs in — a coin flip that is taken once Friday's report confirms he plays.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Love's back keeps him out: Golden (16.9) and Jacobs both lose their quarterback, and Furia Regia's own Love start goes with him — the swing is roughly even, so Golden's fallback (Worthy) is the lever.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Furia Regia still carry McLaurin (season-ending, OUT) in a starting slot; if they swap Jefferson in it is about 18.6 on their side.

doFirst.title: Upgrade to Josh Jacobs only if Friday clears him
doFirst.subtitle: Practised and off Green Bay's injury report; Rapoport expects him to play (Packernet 22 Oct). A clean Friday report means the projection's 0.9 edge is taken.

case.label: The player
case.body: Off the Exempt List Monday; practised Wednesday and is not on Green Bay's official injury report; Ian Rapoport reports he is expected to play, though Jacobs says he doesn't know yet (Packernet 22 Oct 11:40Z). LaFleur: 'pretty good spot', but 'he's missed the exposure to football' — Green Bay could activate him and limit his carries (NFL.com, week of 19 Oct). ESPN still carries a DAY_TO_DAY tag.

case.label: Contested
case.body: Rapoport and FLM say he plays; LaFleur leaves room for a managed workload in his first game of the season. Playing is the likely case; full volume is not. Inside the 2-point line, so the projection decides — once his status is confirmed.

case.label: The timing
case.body: Gordon kicks off at 11:00; Green Bay's inactives come at 12:55. If Jacobs starts and is inactive, no running back on this bench can replace him.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Friday's Packers report shows no designation for Jacobs and LaFleur confirms he plays. Any designation, or no clear word by Sunday 10:30, and Gordon stays.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The swap is made and Gordon outscores Jacobs (archive).

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup tool's Jacobs contingency would fire too late
whatWentWrong.lead: It says check at 12:55 Sunday; Gordon's game starts at 11:00.

case.label: What happened
case.body: lineup_check.py prints 'if inactive at Sun 12:55 CDMX, start Gordon' — but Gordon is locked by then. Followed literally, an inactive Jacobs scores zero.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Gordon stays in; Jacobs comes in only on Friday's evidence (the card above). Golden's contingency does not have the problem: Worthy plays at 18:20.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: ESPN's lock in this league is per-slot rather than per-player — it is not; a started player cannot be benched.

whatWentWrong.sources: lineup_check.py output · ESPN league file kickoffs

whatWentWrong.title: Week 6 was won with 9.9 left on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: Stroud's 23.0 sat behind Daniels's 19.0; Worthy's 14.3 behind Garrett Wilson's 8.4.

case.label: The numbers
case.body: 150.8 to 88.62 over Los Cachanillas; best possible 160.7 (week-6 archive, recomputed this run).

case.label: The lesson
case.body: Both were projection calls that lost — no override, nothing to fix but to keep starting by projection, which is why Rice's card waits on practice rather than on a hunch.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: A projection-set Week 7 lineup leaves more than 15 points on the bench (archive).
